models.title: Unemployment as a fraction of the labor force
models.summary: The unemployment rate compares actively job-seeking unemployed people with the labor force rather than the whole population.

relationship.locator: What are the unemployment rate, labor force participation rate, and employment-population ratio?
relationship.translation_notes: Person_count/person_count gives a base fraction. This ratio is a defined labor-market indicator, distinct from generic relative frequency because its statistical inclusion rules are integral to the quantity meaning. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

models.title: Labor-force participation within a declared population cohort
models.summary: Participation compares labor-force members with the full population in a defined working-age cohort.

relationship.locator: What are the unemployment rate, labor force participation rate, and employment-population ratio?
relationship.translation_notes: Both counts must use exactly the same age and residency definition; no implicit conversion between CFA and BLS coverage. Person counts cancel; percentage display remains external. The inverse labor-force=population*participation also covers the population/participation portion of LM3 Exhibit28. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

variables.definition: Covered cohort members employed or actively seeking and available for work

variables.context: Same date, geographic area and explicitly declared age/civilian/institutional cohort; employed/unemployed are mutually exclusive and use one statistical definition

variables.definition: Share of covered population in the labor force
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: labor force is a subset of the declared population cohort.
Application profile: fix the cohort before binding; CFA illustration says ages16-64 while US BLS uses civilian noninstitutional people16and over with no upper age limit.
limitations: The cohort discrepancy does not change ratio arithmetic but prevents direct unqualified comparison of series.
Retirees and students are not categorically excluded if they meet the chosen employment/seeking-work definition.

models.title: Laspeyres bilateral price index
models.summary: The reading constructs a laspeyres bilateral price index by valuing one base-period basket at current and base prices.

relationship.translation_notes: Both sums have currency dimensions, yielding a base-one price ratio. Published base100 scaling is a display convention and not inlined. Laspeyres and Paasche define distinct basket weighting quantities, even though their evaluated sum-ratio serialization is the same. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.
